scope: Native Anthropic enrichment batches; not full M4 acceptance
checks: Native inline batches use the official SDK and the existing policy-owned transport, with configured credentials, bounded deadlines, no SDK retries and no SDK telemetry.
The existing durable workflow holds budgets before submission, resumes known ids, fences publication and handles per-item results through the same document parser.
Opaque 64-character custom ids map back to original work ids; long local job ids remain valid without leaking their original spelling.
Declared caching, adaptive reasoning and structured output map to native fields. Unsupported size constraints remain in schema descriptions and are still enforced by the core result validator.
Result collection uses the fixed SDK route, never the returned results_url. Byte/line/count/identity bounds, partial outcomes and unknown usage are checked.
Native batch deletion tolerates an already-deleted response. Lifecycle-only bindings cannot submit new inference.
Inline staging survives an interruption before submission. Unknown submissions fail after the existing reconciliation window without automatic resubmission or refund.
All 38 Anthropic adapter cases also passed with synthetic ambient SDK credentials and headers present.
limitations: The native API exposes no batch-level client-key lookup or submission idempotency guarantee. A lost create response remains unconfirmed and fails conservatively after 48 hours rather than scanning unrelated results or creating a duplicate.
No live Anthropic account was used. New adapter results are controlled local HTTP responses; storage checks use a controlled batch provider.

Verified span-level citation integration remains unfinished. Operational deployment, full sustained-write restore, mounted/large-corpus, signed-release and remaining real-export acceptance remain open.
